title: The inclusion $\mathcal O_{E,X}\to E_X$
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, let $E\subseteq\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ be a finite extension of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and let $\mathcal O_E$ be its ring of integers, as in [def-sfb-integers-to-subfield-point]. For a scheme $X$, define
$$
\varphi=p_X^*(a)\colon\mathcal O_{E,X}=p_X^*\underline{\mathcal O}_E\longrightarrow E_X=p_X^*\underline E,
$$
where $a\colon\underline{\mathcal O}_E\to\underline E$ is the condensed inclusion of [def-sfb-integers-to-subfield-point] and $p_X^*$ is the inverse image of [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point]. This is a morphism of ring objects of $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$ between the pulled-back coefficient rings of [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients].

proof.text: By [def-sfb-integers-to-subfield-point], the inclusion $\mathcal O_E\hookrightarrow E$ gives a specified morphism $a\colon\underline{\mathcal O}_E\to\underline E$ of ring objects in $\Sh(*_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$. We use this morphism, whose map on a profinite set $S$ is postcomposition with the inclusion $\mathcal O_E\hookrightarrow E$.

source.place: Definition and proof: the morphism at the point; def-sfb-integers-to-subfield-point

proof.text:
Set $F=p_X^*$, the strong monoidal inverse image functor supplied by [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point], part 4. Apply the ring-object coefficient functor of [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] to the morphism $a$ of step 1 and define $\varphi=F(a)$. Its source is $F\underline{\mathcal O}_E=\mathcal O_{E,X}$ and its target is $F\underline E=E_X$ by that coefficient-ring definition. Explicitly, write $\delta$ and $\epsilon$ for the tensor and unit comparison maps of $F$, and write $\mu_A,\eta_A$ and $\mu_B,\eta_B$ for the ring structures of $A=\underline{\mathcal O}_E$ and $B=\underline E$. Since $a$ preserves multiplication and unit [def-sfb-integers-to-subfield-point], naturality of $\delta$ and functoriality give
$$
F(a)\circ\mu_{A,X}=F(a\circ\mu_A)\circ\delta_{A,A}=F(\mu_B)\circ F(a\otimes a)\circ\delta_{A,A}=\mu_{B,X}\circ(F(a)\otimes F(a)),
\qquad
F(a)\circ\eta_{A,X}=F(a\circ\eta_A)\circ\epsilon=F(\eta_B)\circ\epsilon=\eta_{B,X}.
$$
These are exactly the two ring-object morphism conditions for $\varphi$.
